cases.name: help
cases.stdout:
Drive terminals owned by the podd daemon

Usage: pod.exe [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  run           Start a program in a new terminal (kept alive by a holder process) and print its id
  ls            List terminals (exited ones only with --all)
  keep          Keep an exited terminal from being removed by the retention policy (--unkeep returns it to the policy)
  send          Type text into a terminal, followed by Enter unless --no-enter. Enter is pressed once the program has taken the text in; for an agent the daemon then checks that a turn started and presses Enter once more if not (a warning is printed when it still did not)
  keys          Press named keys: enter, tab, esc, up, ctrl+c, alt+x, f5, ... or single characters
  read          Print the screen (or scrollback + screen with --history)
  wait          Wait until the program exits (default) or the output contains TEXT (the echo of text sent with `pod send` does not count), or for an agent status (--status, --turn-end)
  resize        Resize a terminal (the most recent resize wins, also over attached clients)
  attach        Attach this console to a terminal: raw input and output, Ctrl+] detaches
  status        Show a terminal's agent status
  ack           Acknowledge a terminal (the user saw it): done becomes idle
  hooks         Agent hook configuration
  kill          Kill a terminal's whole process tree
  rm            Forget an exited terminal (ends its holder). --force kills it first
  repo          Registered git repositories (tasks are created in them)
  task          Tasks: a git worktree on branch pod/<name> plus the terminal(s) working in it
  review        Review comments on a task's diff, sent to its agent (P4)
  group         Fan-out groups: one prompt, several agents, compare and pick (P5)
  orch          Orchestration for agents: runs, items, workers, mail (docs/19)
  gate          Human approval gates (P5). Agents call `pod gate request` from their terminal
  pr            A task's GitHub pull request: push, create, status, merge, open (docs/15)
  sessions      Agent sessions found on this PC (Claude Code, Codex): list, resume, link (docs/18)
  mobile        Paired phones: permissions per task, revoke, audit (docs/17; no network listener yet)
  server        Daemon control
  remote-stdio  Bridge stdin/stdout to this user's podd for a remote client (`ssh -T host pod remote-stdio`). Starts the installed podd if none runs. stdout carries protocol lines only; exits when either side closes, leaving the daemon and its terminals running
  machine       SSH machine profiles for `pod --machine <name> …` (docs/17 R3)
  guide         Guides for agents in Pod terminals, matched to this version (`pod guide orchestration`); no topic: the list
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json            Print machine-readable JSON instead of text
      --pipe <PIPE>     Pipe name or path (default: $POD_SOCKET, else \\.\pipe\podd-<username>)
      --machine <NAME>  Run the command on this SSH machine profile (`pod machine add`) instead of the local daemon
  -h, --help            Print help
  -V, --version         Print version

cases.name: help orch
cases.stdout:
Orchestration for agents: runs, items, workers, mail (docs/19)

Usage: pod.exe orch [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  run      Runs: one objective and its coordinator
  item     Work items of a run (with dependencies)
  worker   Start or supervise one worker (attempt)
  workers  Workers of your run (or --run, or every run outside a Pod terminal)
  queue    Workers waiting for resources (FIFO), the limits and measurements
  limits   Resource limits of the worker queue (daemon settings; an environment variable still wins). No flags: show them
  gate     Decision gates of a run (docs/19 §4.5)
  send     Send a message (workers: to their coordinator by default)
  check    Read your unread mail (marks it read)
  reply    Answer a message (questions get an `answer`)
  ask      Workers: ask the coordinator and wait for the answer
  done     Workers: report completion, exactly once
  wait     Workers: wait for other items of your run to finish (e.g. the one whose branch you build on), then end your turn. Not a missed done: Pod mails you when they all finished
  commit   Workers: commit in your own worktree through Pod (hooks off). Codex workers use this instead of `git add`/`git commit`, which their sandbox does not allow
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --json            Print machine-readable JSON instead of text
      --pipe <PIPE>     Pipe name or path (default: $POD_SOCKET, else \\.\pipe\podd-<username>)
